docs.title: Alpaca Connectors
docs.text:
This project publishes Alpaca US equity data into MainSequence.

Current scope:

  • register MainSequence public assets from Alpaca symbols through FIGI
  • extract ETF holdings from published provider sources
  • create holdings-based AssetCategory objects such as HOLDINGS__IVV
  • publish Alpaca stock bars through a MainSequence DataNode
  • schedule recurring bar updates through scheduled_jobs.yaml

docs.title: Repository Areas
docs.text:
• src/assets/: asset registration, FIGI resolution, Alpaca universe checks
  • src/cli/: project CLI commands for assets and holdings categories
  • src/jobs/: repository-local job launchers for scheduled execution paths
  • etf_extraction/extractors/: ETF provider holdings extraction only
  • etf_extraction/service.py: standalone ETF seed expansion service
  • etf_extraction/holdings_categories.py: ETF-owned holdings AssetCategory planning and sync
  • src/data_nodes/: Alpaca stock bars DataNode
  • scripts/: remaining helper entrypoints that are not yet in the CLI
  • etf_extraction/data/seed_universes.yaml: seed universes and ETF provider mapping

docs.title: ETF Extraction Documentation
docs.text:
ETF extraction has its own standalone architecture page:

  • docs/etf_extraction.md

Use that page first when the question is about:

  • provider extraction behavior
  • seed expansion
  • ETF-owned holdings category sync
  • the boundary between ETF logic and Alpaca logic

docs.title: Main Decisions
docs.text:
• Assets are registered in MainSequence by FIGI, not as custom assets.
  • ETF holdings extraction is provider-driven and explicit.
  • Component extraction only happens when both a seed ticker and provider are supplied.
  • Holdings categories are ETF-owned: ETF extraction defines category membership, and only MainSequence asset registration ambiguity/missing assets block category sync.
  • Alpaca daily bars share one table per frequency_id, feed, and adjustment.
  • Daily bar time_index is normalized to 16:00 America/New_York on the session date as a project convention.

docs.title: Build The Docs
docs.text:
uv run mkdocs serve

or:

uv run mkdocs build

docs.title: Related Entry Points
docs.text:
• alpaca-connectors asset register
  • alpaca-connectors holdings-category create
  • alpaca-connectors bars run
  • alpaca-connectors asset <ticker> update_prices <period>
  • src/jobs/run_daily_stock_bars_holdings_ivv.py
  • scheduled_jobs.yaml

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The project previously created ETF holdings AssetCategory objects by passing extracted ETF holdings through Alpaca availability checks, FIGI resolution, and MainSequence asset registration checks before category sync.

That mixed two separate concerns:

  • ETF holdings truth: what symbols belong to an ETF according to the ETF provider
  • Alpaca execution truth: what symbols can be consumed by Alpaca registration or Alpaca bars workflows

Those are not the same boundary.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
ETF holdings categories are owned by etf_extraction.

The ETF holdings category flow is:

  1. ETF ticker identifies a holdings universe.
  2. ETF extraction resolves component symbols from the provider source.
  3. ETF category planning looks up those symbols in MainSequence assets.
  4. If the symbols are registered uniquely in MainSequence, the ETF-owned AssetCategory is synced.

Alpaca is not part of ETF category construction.

Alpaca validation happens later, when Alpaca-specific consumers read assets from the category.

This decision also implies two follow-on rules:

  1. ETF provider configuration and seed-universe configuration belong to etf_extraction.
  2. ETF routine orchestration must call ETF and Alpaca services directly, rather than routing through CLI argument strings.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive:

  • ETF holdings categories remain faithful to ETF source data.
  • Alpaca limitations do not redefine ETF membership.
  • The same ETF AssetCategory can be reused by non-Alpaca consumers.
  • The architecture becomes cleaner: etf_extraction owns ETF universe construction, src/ owns Alpaca validation and bars execution.

Tradeoffs:

  • ETF category sync still requires assets to exist in MainSequence, because AssetCategory stores assets, not raw ticker strings.
  • A category may be blocked by missing or ambiguous MainSequence assets even when ETF extraction itself succeeded.
  • ETF routine execution becomes more explicit in code, which is cleaner architecturally but means orchestration logic now lives in a dedicated service layer instead of being hidden behind CLI indirection.

docs.title: Implementation Boundary
docs.text:
etf_extraction owns:

  • provider inference
  • ETF holdings extraction
  • ETF provider settings
  • seed-universe configuration
  • holdings category planning
  • holdings category sync
  • ETF maintenance orchestration

src/assets owns:

  • Alpaca symbol lookup
  • Alpaca availability checks
  • FIGI resolution
  • MainSequence asset registration from Alpaca symbols

src/data_nodes owns:

  • consuming explicit assets or categories for Alpaca bars updates
  • resolving whether category members can be used with Alpaca

src/cli owns:

  • operator-facing argument parsing
  • translating CLI input into service calls
  • presenting summaries and execution output

It does not own ETF extraction logic or Alpaca registration logic directly.

docs.title: Routine Runner Boundary
docs.text:
ETF maintenance routines are orchestration, not business logic.

The routine runner should compose these steps directly:

  1. ETF expansion service
  2. Alpaca registration service
  3. ETF holdings-category sync service
  4. Alpaca bars execution service

The routine runner should not rebuild CLI command strings and re-enter the application through main(argv).

That pattern hides the true dependencies, makes dry-run output less meaningful, and couples orchestration to presentation-oriented CLI code.

docs.title: Settings Boundary
docs.text:
src/settings.py is the Alpaca/OpenFIGI/MainSequence runtime settings module.

etf_extraction/settings.py is the ETF extraction settings module.

That split means:

  • Alpaca registration and Alpaca bars code do not import ETF provider URL patterns.
  • ETF extraction code does not need to depend on Alpaca credential/runtime settings.
  • the dependency direction is easier to reason about: ETF concerns depend on ETF settings, Alpaca concerns depend on Alpaca/OpenFIGI settings, orchestration composes both.

docs.title: Category Consumer Boundary
docs.text:
HOLDINGS__<ETF> means:

  • the ETF provider says these are the holdings
  • MainSequence has assets registered for those holdings

It does not mean:

  • Alpaca can price every member
  • Alpaca can resolve every member without filtering

Those checks belong to category consumers such as Alpaca bars execution.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: This decision means HOLDINGS__<ETF> represents ETF holdings membership, not "Alpaca-usable ETF holdings membership".

docs.title: ADR: ms-markets Currency Pair Asset Model
Status
docs.text: Proposed

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
This repository is starting a migration from the legacy Main Sequence asset usage toward the newer ms-markets asset model.

The current ms-markets asset design is intentionally narrow:

  • AssetTable stores canonical asset identity
  • AssetTypeTable stores the asset-type registry
  • instrument-specific fields should live in relational detail tables keyed to the asset row

That design is documented in the current ms-markets asset docs and matches the current source:

  • AssetTable keeps uid, unique_identifier, and asset_type
  • AssetTypeTable registers discoverable type strings such as crypto or equity
  • extension data should be modeled through one-to-one detail tables rather than by widening AssetTable

The migration needs a first-class way to represent currency pairs such as BTC/USDT.

That representation must satisfy these requirements:

  • the tradable pair itself must have a canonical asset identity
  • the pair must reference the canonical asset rows for its base and quote legs
  • the leg references must point back to the main asset list, not to free-form strings
  • the design must fit the ms-markets extension pattern instead of adding pair-specific columns to AssetTable

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Currency-pair assets will be modeled as canonical Asset rows plus a one-to-one relational detail table.

The first migration decision is:

  1. Register an asset type with key currency and display name Currency.
  2. Represent a tradable pair such as BTC/USDT as an Asset row whose canonical unique_identifier is the ordered pair string.
  3. Add a CurrencyPairDetailsTable keyed by that pair asset.
  4. Store base_asset_uid and quote_asset_uid on the detail table as foreign keys to AssetTable.uid.
  5. Treat the pair asset row as the canonical identity of the tradable pair, while the referenced base and quote assets remain the canonical identity rows for the underlying legs.

Example:

  • asset BTC
  • asset USDT
  • asset BTC/USDT
  • BTC/USDT has asset_type="currency"
  • CurrencyPairDetailsTable(asset_uid=<BTC/USDT>, base_asset_uid=<BTC>, quote_asset_uid=<USDT>)

docs.title: Relational Shape
docs.text:
The intended schema shape is:

+-----------------------------+        one-to-one pair detail     +-------------------------------+
| AssetTable                  |---------------------------------->| CurrencyPairDetailsTable      |
|-----------------------------|        asset_uid PK/FK            |-------------------------------|
| uid                  PK     |                                   | asset_uid              PK/FK  |
| unique_identifier    unique |                                   | base_asset_uid           FK   |
| asset_type                 |                                   | quote_asset_uid          FK   |
+-----------------------------+                                   +-------------------------------+
          ^                                                                  |
          |                                                                  |
          +--------------------------- foreign keys --------------------------+
                         to canonical leg assets in AssetTable

Expected identifiers:

  • leg asset BTC
  • leg asset USDT
  • pair asset BTC/USDT

Expected foreign-key meaning:

  • asset_uid: the pair asset row
  • base_asset_uid: the base leg asset row
  • quote_asset_uid: the quote leg asset row

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
The migration should preserve these invariants:

  1. AssetTable remains small. Pair semantics do not add base_asset or quote_asset columns directly to AssetTable.
  2. Currency-pair identity is explicit. The tradable pair has its own canonical Asset row.
  3. Pair legs are relational, not textual. Base and quote legs reference canonical asset rows through foreign keys.
  4. Pair direction matters. BTC/USDT and USDT/BTC are different ordered pairs and must not collapse into one record.
  5. Duplicate pair definitions are not allowed. The detail table should enforce uniqueness for the ordered (base_asset_uid, quote_asset_uid) combination.
  6. A pair cannot reference the same asset on both sides. The implementation should reject base_asset_uid == quote_asset_uid.

docs.title: Asset Type Rule
docs.text:
This ADR introduces currency as the registered asset-type key for the first currency-pair slice.

Use:

  • asset_type = "currency"
  • AssetType.display_name = "Currency"

Important current ms-markets detail:

  • in the current release, Asset.asset_type is a string classification field
  • it is logically aligned to AssetType
  • it is not a database foreign key yet

This ADR does not require the leg assets themselves to settle all future type questions today. What is decided now is the pair contract:

  • the pair row is classified as currency
  • the pair row owns the canonical tradable-pair identity
  • the pair row references two canonical leg assets

Whether a leg asset such as BTC or USDT is also classified as currency, crypto, or some other future subtype can be decided in a later ADR if needed.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive:

  • The design matches the documented ms-markets extension model.
  • Pair identity is explicit and queryable as a normal asset.
  • Base and quote legs remain normalized against the canonical asset registry.
  • The same leg assets can be reused across many pairs.
  • Future pair-specific metadata can be added to the detail table without widening AssetTable.

Tradeoffs:

  • Creating one tradable pair now requires at least three coordinated asset records: base asset, quote asset, and pair asset.
  • Pair lookup logic must decide whether callers are asking for a leg asset or a pair asset.
  • A later API/repository layer will need explicit helpers for pair creation and validation; generic Asset.upsert(...) alone is not sufficient to enforce pair invariants.

docs.title: Migration Boundary
docs.text:
This ADR decides only the relational asset-model shape for currency pairs.

It does not yet decide:

  • the exact repository helper names
  • the exact msm.api row model names
  • provider-specific symbol normalization rules
  • price routing or translation-table behavior
  • venue-specific details for FX, crypto, or derivatives exchanges
  • whether existing Alpaca-specific asset registration flows should be retained, wrapped, or replaced

Those decisions should follow after this schema direction is accepted.

docs.title: Follow-On Implementation Shape
docs.text:
When this ADR is implemented, the expected ms-markets layering should be:

  • msm.models.assets.currency_pairs defines CurrencyPairDetailsTable
  • msm.api.assets exposes a typed row model such as CurrencyPairDetails
  • msm.repositories owns compiled create/update/search operations
  • project code under src/ uses those ms-markets assets instead of introducing a parallel local asset schema

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: BTC/USDT is the motivating example for this ADR, but the same pattern is intended for any quoted currency pair whose identity is defined by ordered base and quote assets.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
This project is prepared for Main Sequence project-to-agent workflows through local project instructions, project-specific skills, and an agent card that describe the existing supported repository surface.

This page documents the local agent-ready artifacts only.

It does not claim a live platform release path or a standalone local agent.py runtime.

docs.title: Local Agent Artifacts
docs.text:
• AGENTS.md
  • .agents/skills/
  • .agents/agent_card.json

These files describe how an agent should understand and operate on the repository's existing capabilities.

docs.title: Supported Agent Task Boundary
docs.text:
The local agent-ready surface is intentionally limited to workflows already implemented by the repository:

  • strict Alpaca asset registration
  • ETF holdings-category planning and sync
  • Alpaca stock-bar planning and update workflows
  • the existing thin FastAPI support surface

The project does not claim unsupported local agent actions such as:

  • trading
  • portfolio management
  • arbitrary platform release creation
  • runtime behaviors that are not represented by the current CLI, services, API, or docs

docs.title: Skill Mapping
docs.text:
Project-specific non-Main Sequence skills live under .agents/skills/ and currently cover:

  • asset_registration
  • holdings_category
  • stock_bars
  • application_surfaces/api_surfaces

These skills are meant to describe and support the existing project workflows rather than invent new ones.

docs.title: Agent Card Notes
docs.text:
The agent card lives at:

  • .agents/agent_card.json

The card currently uses the scaffold template structure required by the project-to-agent skill.

Because this repository does not yet declare a concrete local agent runtime endpoint, the interface and provider URLs in the card should be treated as template placeholders until the deployment model is explicitly chosen and verified.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
The project includes a FastAPI surface for automating:

  • asset discovery
  • asset registration
  • single-ticker registration for Command Center AppComponents
  • lightweight charts OHLC spec generation for Command Center rendering
  • holdings-category synchronization

Main files:

  • api/app/main.py
  • api/app/schemas.py
  • api/app/services.py

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
The API is intentionally thin.

  • route handlers validate input and return typed responses
  • service functions call the existing logic under src/
  • the API does not rebuild the Alpaca, FIGI, extractor, or category workflows

docs.title: Health
docs.text: GET /health

docs.title: Discovery configuration
docs.text:
GET /v1/discovery/config

Returns:

  • supported component providers
  • ETF provider map
  • configured seed universes

docs.title: Execute asset registration
docs.text:
POST /v1/assets/registration/execute

This runs the FIGI-based registration flow and creates missing MainSequence public assets.

docs.title: AppComponent single-ticker registration
docs.text:
POST /v1/app-components/assets/register-ticker

This is the AppComponent-facing operation for registering exactly one asset by ticker.

It intentionally uses the default generated AppComponent form instead of a custom editable form.

docs.title: Lightweight Charts OHLC payload
docs.text:
POST /v1/charts/lightweight/ohlc

This endpoint has two modes.

Command Center selector mode:

  • ticker query parameter only

Selector mode returns items and pagination for the AppComponent select2 async ticker search. Each item exposes a user-facing ticker label, a platform unique_identifier, and display text.

Chart mode accepts Command Center query parameters only.

Command Center query fields:

  • ticker, containing the selected ticker, FIGI, or asset unique identifier
  • start_date
  • end_date

The generated workspace form defaults to NVDA, an end date equal to the workspace generation date, and a start date one year before that end date.

In Command Center query mode, the selected ticker value is resolved strictly inside the configured AssetCategory before bars are queried. The API uses the fixed OHLC DataNode identifier alpaca_stock_bars_1d_sip_all; the form does not expose DataNode or unique identifier inputs.

Returns:

  • structured spec object matching the lightweight-charts-spec widget format

Both selector mode and chart mode use the same explicit FastAPI response-body schema: LightweightOhlcResponse. The mode field identifies whether the payload contains selector results or chart data.

docs.title: Execute holdings category sync
docs.text:
POST /v1/holdings-categories/execute

This creates or refreshes the holdings AssetCategory from ETF extraction after MainSequence asset lookup passes.

docs.title: Local Run
docs.text: uv run uvicorn api.app.main:app --reload

docs.title: Important Boundary
docs.text:
The ETF extractor logic and holdings-category logic are owned by etf_extraction/. Alpaca registration and Alpaca bars logic remain owned by src/. The API is only the HTTP contract over those services.

This API does not add LoggedUserContextMiddleware because the current routes do not consume request-local MainSequence user context.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
etf_extraction/ is a standalone package for ETF holdings workflows.

It owns:

  • provider-specific holdings extraction
  • ETF seed expansion into component symbols
  • ETF provider configuration and seed-universe data
  • ETF-owned holdings AssetCategory planning and sync
  • ETF-oriented tests

It does not own:

  • Alpaca symbol validation
  • Alpaca asset registration
  • Alpaca bars DataNode execution
  • generic CLI/runtime settings for the rest of the project

That separation is intentional. ETF holdings are a source dataset. Alpaca is one downstream consumer.

docs.title: Root Package
docs.text:
Repository path:

etf_extraction/

Main modules:

  • etf_extraction/service.py
  • etf_extraction/settings.py
  • etf_extraction/holdings_categories.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/
  • etf_extraction/data/seed_universes.yaml
  • etf_extraction/tests/

docs.title: ETF expansion service
docs.text:
Defined in etf_extraction/service.py.

Primary API:

  • EtfExpansionRequest
  • EtfExpansionResult
  • expand_etf_seed_symbols(...)

Responsibility:

  • receive one or more seed tickers plus an explicit provider
  • build the correct extractor
  • return the expanded symbol universe

Output shape:

  • EtfExpansionResult.component_provider
  • EtfExpansionResult.universe
  • EtfExpansionResult.symbols_for_registration

This service is independent of Alpaca. It only expands ETF seeds into symbols.

docs.title: Holdings category service
docs.text:
Defined in etf_extraction/holdings_categories.py.

Primary API:

  • build_holdings_asset_category_unique_identifier(...)
  • infer_holdings_component_provider(...)
  • build_holdings_asset_category_plan(...)
  • resolve_existing_assets_by_ticker(...)
  • sync_holdings_asset_category(...)

Plan object:

  • HoldingsAssetCategoryPlan

Sync result:

  • AssetCategorySyncResult

Responsibility:

  • infer or receive the ETF provider
  • extract component symbols for one ETF
  • check which symbols already map to existing MainSequence assets
  • detect missing or ambiguous MainSequence ticker matches
  • create or refresh the ETF-owned AssetCategory

Important boundary:

  • this service does not call Alpaca
  • this service does not require Alpaca tradability checks
  • this service only depends on ETF extraction plus MainSequence asset/category state

docs.title: Provider Extraction Layer
docs.text:
Extractor implementations live under etf_extraction/extractors/.

Modules:

  • etf_extraction/extractors/common.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/registry.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/browser.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/ishares.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/invesco.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/vanguard.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/state_street.py

The extractor layer owns:

  • provider URL resolution
  • provider response fetching
  • provider-specific parsing
  • normalization into ExpandedSymbolUniverse

The extractor layer does not own:

  • MainSequence asset registration
  • Alpaca API interaction
  • AssetCategory sync

docs.title: Configuration And Seed Data
docs.text:
ETF-specific settings live in etf_extraction/settings.py.

This module owns:

  • SUPPORTED_COMPONENT_PROVIDERS
  • ETF_EXTRACTION_DIR
  • ETF_DATA_DIR
  • SEED_UNIVERSES_PATH
  • get_seed_universes()
  • get_etf_provider_map()
  • ETF_PROVIDER_MAP_NORMALIZED
  • provider source builders such as get_ishares_holdings_source(...)

Seed-universe data lives in:

etf_extraction/data/seed_universes.yaml

That file is the source for:

  • etf_provider_map_normalized
  • ETF ticker groups such as etfs_main_tickers
  • other ETF-owned symbol lists used by the extraction side

docs.title: Seed expansion only
docs.text:
Used when a caller needs component symbols but does not need category sync yet.

Flow:

  1. caller creates EtfExpansionRequest
  2. expand_etf_seed_symbols(...) validates the provider
  3. the provider extractor expands the seed tickers
  4. the caller receives explicit component symbols

Typical downstream consumer:

  • src/cli/asset.py, which expands ETF seeds first and then passes explicit symbols into the Alpaca registration flow

docs.title: Holdings category creation
docs.text:
Used when a caller needs an ETF-owned AssetCategory such as HOLDINGS__IVV.

Flow:

  1. ETF ticker is normalized
  2. provider is inferred from ETF_PROVIDER_MAP_NORMALIZED or supplied explicitly
  3. extractor expands the ETF into component symbols
  4. MainSequence asset lookup checks whether those symbols already exist uniquely
  5. sync_holdings_asset_category(...) creates or refreshes HOLDINGS__<ETF>

Important detail:

  • this flow is about ETF membership
  • it is not an Alpaca availability filter

If Alpaca later cannot use some members of the category, that is handled by Alpaca consumers, not by etf_extraction/

docs.title: Overlap With Alpaca
docs.text:
The overlap is intentionally narrow.

etf_extraction/ produces:

  • explicit component tickers
  • ETF-owned holdings categories

src/ consumes those outputs for Alpaca-specific work:

  • src/cli/asset.py uses ETF expansion output before Alpaca registration planning
  • src/assets/alpaca_us_equities.py handles Alpaca plus FIGI registration from explicit symbols only
  • src/data_nodes/alpaca_bars.py consumes existing assets or categories and decides what Alpaca bars can publish

Dependency direction:

etf_extraction -> explicit symbols or HOLDINGS__<ETF> category
src/ Alpaca code -> validates or consumes those outputs later

That means ETF extraction can be reasoned about independently from Alpaca runtime constraints.

docs.title: CLI Surfaces That Use ETF Extraction
docs.text:
ETF expansion for registration:

alpaca-connectors asset register --seed-tickers IVV --component-provider ishares

ETF category planning and sync:

alpaca-connectors holdings-category create --etf-ticker IVV
alpaca-connectors holdings-category create --etf-ticker IVV --execute

These commands are orchestration layers. The ETF logic itself lives under etf_extraction/.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
ETF-specific tests live under:

etf_extraction/tests/

Current coverage areas:

  • extractor behavior
  • ETF holdings category planning
  • ETF routine orchestration

This keeps ETF regression coverage close to the ETF-owned package instead of mixing it into Alpaca-only test modules.

docs.title: ETF Holdings Extractors
docs.text:
See also:

  • docs/etf_extraction.md for the standalone ETF extraction architecture and package boundary

docs.title: Scope Boundary
docs.text:
The extractor layer is independent of MainSequence.

Provider extractors do only one job:

  • read published provider holdings sources
  • parse component tickers
  • return expanded symbol universes

They do not register assets, create categories, or publish DataNodes.

Modules:

  • etf_extraction/extractors/ishares.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/invesco.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/vanguard.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/state_street.py
  • etf_extraction/extractors/registry.py

docs.title: Supported Providers
docs.text:
• ishares
  • invesco
  • vanguard
  • state_street

docs.title: URL Strategy
docs.text: Provider URLs are derived dynamically by ticker and provider pattern. The project does not hardcode a separate static holdings URL for every ETF.

docs.title: Published-Source Rule
docs.text:
The extractors parse what the providers actually publish.

  • prefer official download links or official holdings payloads
  • do not invent hidden URLs when the provider does not publish them
  • browser automation is allowed when the published page requires client-side interaction

docs.title: Browser Support
docs.text:
The repo includes playwright as a dependency because some provider flows need browser-backed fetching.

Install the browser runtime with:

bash scripts/install_browser_runtime.sh

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
alpaca-connectors asset register --seed-tickers IVV --component-provider ishares
alpaca-connectors asset register --seed-tickers QQQ --component-provider invesco
alpaca-connectors asset register --seed-tickers VNQ --component-provider vanguard
alpaca-connectors asset register --seed-tickers SPY --component-provider state_street

docs.title: Important Decision
docs.text: SPY is not treated as an iShares product. If SPY components are needed, they come from the State Street extractor.

docs.title: Holdings Categories
docs.text:
See also:

  • docs/etf_extraction.md for the ETF-owned architecture, provider flow, and separation from Alpaca logic

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Create a MainSequence AssetCategory from an ETF's published holdings.

Main module:

  • etf_extraction/holdings_categories.py

Primary CLI:

  • src/cli/

docs.title: Naming Convention
docs.text:
Holdings categories use:

HOLDINGS__[ETF_TICKER]

Example:

HOLDINGS__IVV

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. infer or receive the ETF holdings provider
  2. extract the ETF component tickers
  3. check that extracted components are already registered as MainSequence assets
  4. detect ambiguous ticker-to-asset matches in MainSequence
  5. create or refresh the AssetCategory

docs.title: Blockers
docs.text:
Category creation is refused when any extracted holding:

  • is not already registered in MainSequence
  • resolves ambiguously to more than one MainSequence asset

docs.title: Provider Inference
docs.text:
The ETF-to-provider mapping is stored in:

  • etf_extraction/data/seed_universes.yaml

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Dry run:

alpaca-connectors holdings-category create --etf-ticker IVV

Execute:

alpaca-connectors holdings-category create --etf-ticker IVV --execute

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Register Alpaca US equity assets in MainSequence strictly through FIGI resolution.

Main module:

  • src/assets/alpaca_us_equities.py

Primary CLI:

  • src/cli/

docs.title: Registration Contract
docs.text:
A symbol is eligible for registration only if:

  1. it exists in the Alpaca US equity universe
  2. it resolves to a FIGI
  3. it is missing from MainSequence when checked by FIGI

If FIGI is missing, the symbol is reported and skipped. There is no fallback custom-asset registration path.

docs.title: Stock vs ETP Classification
docs.text:
The registration plan classifies Alpaca symbols through ordered FIGI passes:

  1. Common Stock
  2. ETP
  3. REIT

The FIGI market-sector and security-type constants are loaded from MainSequence constants through src/settings.py.

docs.title: Environment And Secrets
docs.text:
Alpaca credentials are resolved in this order:

  1. ALPACA_API_KEY / ALPACA_SECRET_KEY from the process environment
  2. MainSequence secrets with the same names

If neither source exists, the code fails fast.

docs.title: Symbol Normalization
docs.text:
The registration path normalizes common class-share aliases when resolving against Alpaca and FIGI, for example:

  • BRKB -> BRK.B
  • BFB -> BF.B

Slash and dash variants are also considered.

docs.title: Exact symbols only
docs.text: alpaca-connectors asset register --symbols AAPL,MSFT,NVDA

docs.title: ETF component expansion
docs.text:
alpaca-connectors asset register --seed-tickers IVV --component-provider ishares

This remains an orchestration flow. ETF expansion is owned by etf_extraction/, and the resulting explicit symbols are then passed into the Alpaca registration service in src/assets/.

docs.title: Strict Extraction Rule
docs.text:
ETF component extraction is only allowed when both are explicitly provided:

  • --seed-tickers
  • --component-provider

Otherwise the script does not expand holdings.

docs.title: Output Reporting
docs.text:
The script reports:

  • symbols missing from Alpaca
  • symbols missing FIGI
  • symbols already registered
  • symbols that would be created on --execute

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
The project includes a Command Center AppComponent configuration for the workspace:

  • Alpaca Assets Registry

This widget is meant to let a user register one Alpaca-backed asset directly by ticker through the project's FastAPI surface.

docs.title: Widget Contract
docs.text:
The mounted widget type is:

  • app-component

The widget is configured against this API route:

  • POST /v1/app-components/assets/register-ticker

That route is intentionally simple:

  • request body: one ticker plus optional operational flags
  • response body: explicit registration result for exactly one ticker

This is an AppComponent flow, not a data-node-table-visualizer flow, so the response is a normal typed FastAPI model instead of a table-widget SDK contract.

docs.title: API Decision
docs.text:
For this widget, the default generated AppComponent form is sufficient.

We did not add a custom EditableFormDefinition because the operation only needs:

  • ticker
  • include_non_tradable
  • timeout

That matches the Command Center rule to prefer autogenerated forms unless the UX truly needs custom sections or field-level specialization.

docs.title: Workspace Builder
docs.text:
The repo owns the workspace payload builder in:

  • src/command_center/workspaces.py

and a thin file generator in:

  • scripts/build_alpaca_assets_registry_workspace.py

Example:

.venv/bin/python scripts/build_alpaca_assets_registry_workspace.py --fastapi-release-id 701

This writes:

  • command_center/workspaces/alpaca_assets_registry.workspace.yaml

The generated workspace update mounts one widget:

  • title: Register Asset By Ticker
  • widget id: app-component
  • target mode: main-sequence-resource-release
  • operation: POST /v1/app-components/assets/register-ticker

docs.title: Why The Widget Uses A FastAPI Release
docs.text:
The intended workspace target is a deployed MainSequence FastAPI resource release, not a localhost URL.

The widget props therefore use:

  • apiTargetMode: main-sequence-resource-release
  • mainSequenceResourceRelease.releaseId

instead of a hardcoded local apiBaseUrl.

docs.title: Source Of Truth For The Widget Payload
docs.text:
The local skill docs did not include a concrete mounted AppComponent payload example, so the widget payload was verified against the local Command Center frontend source:

  • CommandCenter/src/widgets/core/app-component/definition.ts
  • CommandCenter/src/widgets/core/app-component/appComponentModel.ts

Important confirmed details:

  • widget id is app-component
  • the widget can target a Main Sequence FastAPI resource release directly
  • method, path, and requestBodyContentType are persisted widget props
  • runtime OpenAPI discovery can generate the form from the selected operation

docs.title: Current Limitation
docs.text:
Applying the generated workspace update to the live platform still requires a valid authenticated MainSequence CLI or SDK session.

When auth is available, apply the generated file with:

mainsequence cc workspace update 3 --file command_center/workspaces/alpaca_assets_registry.workspace.yaml

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Publish Alpaca stock OHLCV bars into MainSequence for either:

  • a registered AssetCategory
  • a strict list of registered tickers

Main modules:

  • src/data_nodes/alpaca_bars.py
  • src/data_nodes/alpaca_bars_support.py

Primary runner:

  • src/cli/bars.py

docs.title: Data Contract
docs.text:
The node publishes an asset-indexed table with:

  • index: (time_index, unique_identifier)
  • columns:
  • open
  • high
  • low
  • close
  • volume
  • trade_count
  • vwap

unique_identifier is always the MainSequence asset unique_identifier.

docs.title: Hashed Fields
docs.text:
These fields are part of dataset identity:

  • frequency_id
  • feed
  • adjustment

This prevents mixing sip and iex, or adjusted and unadjusted bars, in the same dataset.

docs.title: Shared Table Identity
docs.text:
The table identity is shared across scopes and depends only on:

  • frequency_id
  • feed
  • adjustment

That means ticker runs and category runs with the same values for those fields append/update the same DataNode table.

docs.title: Asset category mode
docs.text:
alpaca-connectors bars run \
  --asset-category-unique-identifier HOLDINGS__IVV \
  --frequency-id 1d \
  --feed sip \
  --adjustment all

In category mode, the category is assumed to already exist. The Alpaca bars flow loads and consumes the category; it does not create or refresh it.

docs.title: Ticker mode
docs.text:
alpaca-connectors bars run \
  --tickers NVDA \
  --frequency-id 1d \
  --feed sip \
  --adjustment all

docs.title: Shorthand asset mode
docs.text:
alpaca-connectors asset IVV update_prices daily

The shorthand resolves the registered MainSequence asset from ticker IVV, uses the project daily price defaults of feed=sip and adjustment=all, builds the AlpacaStockBarsConfig, and runs the DataNode for that single asset.

Ticker mode is strict. Every ticker must exist in Alpaca and also exist as exactly one registered MainSequence asset.

docs.title: Time Index Decision
docs.text:
For intraday bars, time_index is the right edge of the interval.

For 1d bars, the project normalizes time_index to:

  • 16:00 America/New_York
  • on the same session date

This is a project normalization convention, not a claim that Alpaca guarantees that exact vendor-native final observation timestamp in every case.

docs.title: Incomplete-Bar Handling
docs.text: The updater filters out the current incomplete period before persistence.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
The node resolves Alpaca credentials via:

  1. environment variables
  2. MainSequence secrets fallback

If neither exists, it fails fast.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: uv sync

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Browser Runtime
docs.text:
Some ETF provider extraction paths need browser support.

bash scripts/install_browser_runtime.sh

docs.title: Register assets
docs.text: alpaca-connectors asset register --symbols NVDA,AAPL

docs.title: Register from ETF holdings
docs.text: alpaca-connectors asset register --seed-tickers IVV --component-provider ishares --execute

docs.title: Create holdings category
docs.text:
alpaca-connectors holdings-category create --etf-ticker IVV --execute

This creates or refreshes the ETF-owned holdings category. The fixed Alpaca bars job that targets HOLDINGS__IVV assumes that category already exists before it runs.

docs.title: Run daily bars for a category
docs.text:
alpaca-connectors bars run \
  --asset-category-unique-identifier HOLDINGS__IVV \
  --frequency-id 1d \
  --feed sip \
  --adjustment all

docs.title: Run daily bars for one ticker
docs.text:
alpaca-connectors bars run \
  --tickers NVDA \
  --frequency-id 1d \
  --feed sip \
  --adjustment all

docs.title: Shorthand asset price update
docs.text: alpaca-connectors asset IVV update_prices daily

docs.title: VS Code Launch Configurations
docs.text:
The repo includes launch configurations for:

  • asset registration from IVV
  • holdings-category creation for IVV
  • daily bars for HOLDINGS__IVV
  • daily bars for NVDA

docs.title: Current Job Target
docs.text:
The project includes:

  • scheduled_jobs.yaml
  • src/jobs/run_daily_stock_bars_holdings_ivv.py
  • src/jobs/run_etf_maintenance_routines.py
  • data/etf_maintenance_routines.yaml

Use the routine runner for looped ETF workflows (register, category sync, ETF prices, category prices):

Example:

.venv/bin/python src/jobs/run_etf_maintenance_routines.py --dry-run

Run --dry-run first to verify generated command order, then execute:

.venv/bin/python src/jobs/run_etf_maintenance_routines.py

That launcher runs daily bars for:

  • HOLDINGS__IVV
  • 1d
  • sip
  • all

The fixed src/jobs/run_daily_stock_bars_holdings_ivv.py launcher assumes that HOLDINGS__IVV already exists as a MainSequence AssetCategory. It consumes the category; it does not create or refresh it.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
The current crontab expression is:

0 0 * * *

This means midnight UTC.

docs.title: File Shape
docs.text:
jobs:
  - name: "Alpaca Daily Stock Bars HOLDINGS__IVV"
    execution_path: "src/jobs/run_daily_stock_bars_holdings_ivv.py"
    task_schedule:
      type: "crontab"
      expression: "0 0 * * *"
    related_image_id: 0
    cpu_request: "0.25"
    memory_request: "0.5"

docs.title: Important Operational Note
docs.text:
At the time this documentation was written, the project had no project images available from mainsequence project images list, so related_image_id: 0 is only a placeholder.

Before scheduling the batch for real, a valid project image must exist.

docs.title: Submit The Batch
docs.text: /bin/zsh -lc "set -a; source .env; export MAINSEQUENCE_AUTH_MODE=jwt; set +a; .venv/bin/mainsequence project schedule_batch_jobs scheduled_jobs.yaml"
